name: Rising Spirit
summary: At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers a ritual blessing drawn from Agamaggan's ancient power. Bring blood shards taken from his Bristleback rivals, and he strengthens your will and spirit.

sections.title: Willpower of the Razormane
sections.body: Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth knows the geomancy and ancestral magic of the quilboar. He takes pride in his people's devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. To Mangletooth, an unbroken spirit carries a warrior onward when strength fails and defeat seems near.

sections.title: The Power of Blood Shards
sections.body: Mangletooth asks for blood shards to raise your spirit. These crystals hold Agamaggan's ancient blood, which seeped into the red earth ten thousand years ago. Bring him shards gathered across the Barrens, especially from his Bristleback enemies, and he can channel their power into a blessing that bolsters your will.

faq.answer: Mangletooth is an elder Razormane quilboar held in a wooden cage at Camp Taurajo. Though the Horde keeps him captive, he shares sacred geomantic rites for blood shards and uses travelers to strike at the rival Bristlebacks.

Blood shards are red mineral crystals formed from the blood of Agamaggan, an Ancient Demigod who died in the Barrens during the War of the Ancients. Quilboar shamans and geomancers draw on their lingering magic for boons and rituals.

faq.q: Why does Mangletooth help Horde adventurers?
faq.answer: Mangletooth hates the rival Bristleback quilboar. He trades blessings for blood shards to spur powerful travelers to kill Bristlebacks across the Barrens, carrying on his tribe's feud from behind the cage.

faq.q: What does the Rising Spirit blessing do?
faq.answer: The Rising Spirit blessing from Mangletooth strengthens a warrior's spirit and resolve. It draws on Agamaggan's enduring life force to keep hope alive through hard encounters.

Agamaggan is the colossal Boar Ancient who fought the Burning Legion ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. The quilboar revere him as their creator and believe the Barrens' thorny brambles and red blood shards grew from his fallen body.

faq.q: Is this ritual a one-time trade?
faq.answer: No. Bring Mangletooth four blood shards, and he will perform the ritual again to renew your blessing before you venture into the wastes.

angles.text: As a priest, you may recognize the quilboar's communion with Agamaggan as a raw expression of faith and spirit, rivaling the organized devotions of eastern churches.
As a shaman, you understand how ancient bloodlines and earth minerals can bind the spirits of the land to a mortal warrior.
As a Horde wanderer in the Barrens, you can turn Mangletooth's hatred of the Bristlebacks into a tactical advantage.
